comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
**A sharper argument for the ask than the shell one: the pinned daemon
can be told to unpin itself.** herdr's `version_check` and
`manifest_check` both default to **true**
(`src/config/model.rs::UpdateConfig::default`), so the daemon Muster
ships - named and checksummed in `deps/herdr.pin`, downloaded and
verified by `./dev`, staged inside the app bundle - runs its update
checks according to a config file Muster does not own.

That moves this card off ergonomics. Pinning the daemon is the whole
reason "green suite means it works" means anything: a Muster talking to a
daemon its corpus was never recorded against is a window whose every
behaviour is unverified, which is why `./dev` refuses a daemon whose wire
schema has moved. None of that is enforceable while the pinned binary
takes its update policy from `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`.

Also worth adding to the ask, because it decides between the two options
already listed: **a flag cannot leak, an environment variable has to be
scrubbed.** `herdr server --config <path>` is invisible to a pane by
construction. A `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` would have to be removed from the
environment before spawning each pane, which is a discipline the caller
cannot verify from outside and a regression nobody would notice - the
symptom is a pane reading Muster's daemon config instead of the user's,
which looks like nothing at all until it does.

Muster's side of this is now carded as a_294rihJCP.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
**Correction: the description's central claim is wrong, and this is no
longer a blocker.** It says the per-pane `env` map "is only on that path -
`pane.split`, `tab.create` and `workspace.create` take no env". At the
pinned 0.8.0 all three take one. `PaneSplitParams` carries
`env: HashMap<String, String>` (`src/api/schema/panes.rs:12`), and
`tab.create` (`src/app/api/tabs.rs:73`) and `workspace.create`
(`src/app/api/workspaces.rs:51`) route the same field through the same
`normalize_launch_env`. Verified against `~/src/herdr` at `346411f`, tag
v0.8.0, matching `deps/herdr.pin`.

So Muster can point the daemon at a private config directory after all,
and hand each pane the user's own `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` back as it is
created. The worse fault this card was avoiding does not have to be
accepted. a_294rihJCP now carries the mechanism.

**It also inverts the argument in the comment above.** The reason for
preferring `--config` over `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` was that a flag cannot
leak while an environment variable has to be scrubbed, and scrubbing is a
discipline nobody can verify from outside. Per-pane env is not that: the
restore is a parameter on each pane-creating call, so a conformance case
can assert every pane-creating intent carries it, and a path that forgets
fails the gate rather than leaking silently.

**What the ask is now.** Still worth making, but as ergonomics rather
than as the thing standing between Muster and its own daemon config.
Restoring a variable on every pane-creating call is more machinery than
naming a file once, and it is machinery that has to be right on every
future path that makes a pane.

**One thing the workaround does not reach**, and it is the reason the ask
does not close entirely: `pane.split` reads `self.state.default_shell`
with no per-call override (`src/app/api/panes.rs:57`). What a pane runs is
still whatever the daemon's config says. That is fine once the daemon's
config is Muster's file, which is exactly what the workaround buys - but
it means the fix routes through owning the config rather than through the
API, and an API that let a caller name a pane's command would be a
cleaner answer to the original complaint.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
**The ask is already answered, and has been since before this card was written.**
`HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` is exactly the second option this card proposes - "a `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH`
read only by the server" - and it exists at the pinned 0.8.0. `config_path()` reads it
(`src/config/io.rs:169`), `Config::load()` calls that, and `run_server` calls `Config::load()`
(`src/server/headless.rs:4672`). It is a plain `pub const` at `src/config.rs:38`, not
test-gated, and `herdr --help` prints `Env: HERDR_CONFIG_PATH overrides config file path`.
Both this card and a_294rihJCP say no such variable exists; that was checked twice and wrong
twice.

Better than the description hoped, in the way that matters most here: it moves the config
*file* without moving the config *directory*. The socket comes from `config_dir()`
(`src/session.rs:157-170`), which this does not touch - so Muster's daemon keeps its socket,
its session state and its data directory, and none of the "worse fault than the one it fixes"
applies. Measured against the shipped binary, not just read: a scratch daemon started with it
set read the named file, ignored the `config.toml` in its `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, and bound the
socket the config directory said it would.

**So Muster's half is done** (a_294rihJCP), and what is left of this card is the smaller
ergonomic version of its own argument. The variable is inherited by every pane, and herdr does
not scrub it - `src/pane.rs:112-135` removes `CODEX_THREAD_ID` and adds the `HERDR_*` identity
variables, and leaves this one alone. So `herdr` run inside a Muster pane would read Muster's
daemon config unless Muster puts the user's own path back, which it now does on every
pane-creating call using the per-pane `env` this card's second comment already identified.

That works and is asserted by a conformance case, so this is no longer blocking anything. What
a `herdr server --config <path>` would still buy is that a flag cannot be inherited at all,
which would remove the restore rather than making it checkable. Worth asking for on those
terms - a smaller ask than the one written here, and honestly labelled as ergonomics.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Muster's daemon runs under a herdr session of its own, on a socket of its own, from a binary Muster shipped - and then reads the user's own `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`. A `default_shell` or a `shell_mode` somebody set for their own terminal silently decides what every Muster pane runs, and the corpus Muster is judged against was recorded against neither that config nor any other.

**It cannot be fixed from this side, and that is the ask.** herdr resolves its config directory from `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and nothing else (`src/config/io.rs`, `config_dir` - there is no flag and no `HERDR_CONFIG_*` variable; the only env vars herdr reads are `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `HERDR_CLIENT_SOCKET_PATH`, `HERDR_SESSION`, `HERDR_BIN_PATH`, `HERDR_ENV`, and the three pane identity ones). A pane's process inherits the daemon's environment, so pointing the daemon at a private config directory points every pane's git, editor, gh and shell at one too. That is a worse fault than the one it fixes, so Muster does not do it.

**The ask:** a way to name the config file independently of `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` - `herdr server --config <path>`, or a `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` read only by the server. Either separates "which config this daemon runs on" from "where the programs inside it look for theirs", which are two different questions that share one variable today.

Worth noting there is already a partial answer in the API that does not reach this: `layout.apply` takes a `LayoutNode` carrying a per-pane `env` map, so herdr can already give one pane an environment of its own. It is only on that path - `pane.split`, `tab.create` and `workspace.create` take no env - and applying a layout is not what a keystroke means, so Muster cannot route ordinary pane creation through it to get there.

Until then Muster names the file in its run log at daemon start (`daemon.starting`, `config` field), so a pane that opened an unexpected shell is diagnosable rather than mysterious.

Related: a_28YgGqYq7, whose environment half is fixed - the daemon is now handed an allowlist rather than the launching shell's whole world. This is the half that was left.
title: 🔌 Upstream: a daemon cannot be given a config without giving its panes one
